description:
GOAL: Add the built-in File runtime-library module backed by the resource lifecycle, so fz programs can perform a useful Elixir-shaped filesystem surface without hand-written libc externs.

SIGNAL:
- The real runtime File module is lazy-loadable from the bootstrap registry.
- A behavior fixture exercises create, write, read, open, close, directory, and path operations plus failure tuples across interp, run, and build.
- Explicit close is idempotent with the resource destructor, so a closed descriptor is never closed again after reuse.
- Rust and fixture gates pass with no new warnings.

STRATEGY:
1. Inventory ../elixir/lib/elixir/lib/file.ex against available fz types and runtime ABI, keeping unsupported process, Stream, and File.Stat features out of the claimed surface.
2. Add one process-aware runtime File bridge that owns binary/path conversion, OS error atoms, fz result construction, and descriptor ownership.
3. Layer the public File API and opaque resource handle in lib/file.fz; use make_resource only at the ownership boundary.
4. Replace the local resource fixture stand-in with real File usage and pin a focused filesystem behavior fixture across all execution paths.
5. Document the supported surface and explicit divergences; remove temporary fixture-only File definitions.
title: Runtime library: add File surface
